story: Arjuna, the third Pandava, was the greatest archer of his age. He won Draupadi in a contest by hitting a fish's eye while looking only at its reflection in water. At Kurukshetra he refused to fight his own family, and Krishna's answer became the Bhagavad Gita.
belief: Arjuna is the model seeker: the one who doubts, asks and listens. Anyone who reads the Gita is put in Arjuna's place, and India's top sports award is named after him.
turns: He shot Bhishma from behind Shikhandi, whom Bhishma refused to fight. He killed Karna while Karna was unarmed, trying to free his chariot wheel. And his pride in being the best archer is what cost Ekalavya his thumb.
facts: He spent a year in disguise as Brihannala, a dance teacher.
The Arjuna Award is one of India's highest sporting honours.
